data.narrative:
Quobly is a seed-stage quantum computing company founded by Maud Vinet, Tristan Meunier, and François Perruchot. The quantum computing sector comprises 11 identifiable comparables: 3 public firms (IONQ, RGTI, QBTS) and 8 private companies, including later-stage peers such as Quantinuum, IonQ, D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Infleqtion.

Standard peer-median valuation methodology is not applicable here. The seed-stage segment lacks sufficient comparable datapoints—zero same-stage or adjacent-stage peers meeting screening criteria were identified within the quantum computing universe. While five quantum computing companies exist in the broader comp set, none satisfy the narrow filters required for reliable median-based triangulation (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier). Relying on all-sector medians would conflate seed-stage economics with growth and late-stage profiles, introducing unacceptable distortion.

Without sufficient same-stage or near-stage comparables, traditional comparable-company analysis cannot be responsibly applied. A defensible valuation would require either: (1) expansion to adjacent frontier-tech sectors with stronger seed-stage coverage; (2) reliance on venture capital method or cost-of-capital approaches; or (3) direct market intelligence on recent quantum computing seed rounds. The current data set does not support a triangulated valuation range. Key uncertainty centers on whether seed-stage quantum companies trade at comparable risk-adjusted multiples to other deep-tech verticals, or whether sector-specific technical and commercialization risks warrant material discounting.
